title: Model Catalog Demo - NovaSpring Health
summary: AE + SE walked NovaSpring through Redwood's model catalog UI and API. Focus was on selecting open models for clinical summarization and triage pipelines, benchmark results (latency, token cost, accuracy proxies), quantization/compatibility matrix for GPUs and CPUs, and routing/fallback strategies. Customer asked about SOC 2, VPC private deployment, and getting a pilot for a 2-week benchmark with sample prompts. Next steps: send pricing, share benchmark spreadsheet, schedule pilot kickoff and security docs.
topics: Benchmarks: latency vs. cost vs. quality
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
next_steps: Lena to send tailored pricing and pilot SOP by 2026-06-09
Marcus to share model benchmark spreadsheet and compatibility matrix link (Google Sheet)
Sara to coordinate with Redwood for VPC/network requirements and schedule kickoff call week of 2026-06-15
Customer to provide a small prompt set (50-100) and sample records for benching by 2026-06-10
action_items: Lena Park - Send pricing + trial contract draft - due 2026-06-09
Marcus Li - Upload benchmark spreadsheet and compatibility matrix link - due 2026-06-06
Sara Kim - Provide network contacts + sample prompt set - due 2026-06-10
transcript: 00:00:00 - Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE working with NovaSpring. With me is Marcus (SE) and Jonah who will walk through the model catalog demo today. How's everyone doing?

00:00:10 - Priya Desai: Hey Lena, doing good. Thanks. We have Tom, Sara, and Evan on our side. We want to see how Redwood helps us pick open models for clinical summarization and triage, and how you benchmark them.

00:00:25 - Marcus Li: Great. We'll demo the Console model catalog first — API surface as well — then show bench numbers and a compatibility matrix we use to decide quantization and hardware. We'll also cover routing policies and how to fall back to cheaper variants under load.

00:00:40 - Tom Reynolds: Quick ask before you dive in — we're HIPAA-adjacent in terms of handling PHI in deidentified workflows. Can you touch on the private deployment and VPC options and how they affect latency?

00:00:52 - Lena Park: Yep great question. We'll highlight Dedicated and Private during the demo; dedicated gives predictable throughput, private gives you the control plane in your VPC. Marcus will highlight expected tail latency with private VPC peering as well.

00:01:05 - Jonah Rivera: I'll start with the model catalog UI. Here you can filter by task — summarization, Q&A, embeddings — then by license type, architecture, and performance profile. For NovaSpring we recommend filtering to medically-aligned open models like finetuned Llama variants and specialized bio-med models we've verified.

00:01:22 - 00:01:50 - Jonah Rivera: (screen) You can see each model card shows a quick benchmark: median latency at 128 tokens on A100, cost per 1k tokens, and an accuracy proxy from our evals on public clinical summarization datasets. Note that accuracy proxy is relative — we recommend running your own prompts for final validation.
00:01:51 - Priya Desai: That accuracy proxy — what datasets are those based on? Our summaries are clinician-facing, so small differences matter.

00:02:05 - Marcus Li: We use a mix of MIMIC-derived summarization test sets and some internal prompt sets for clinical triage. It's not a perfect match but gives a head-to-head comparison. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet with per-prompt metrics so you can see variance by prompt length and domain.
00:02:22 - Tom Reynolds: How noisy is the transcription? sorry, the benchmark — how noisy are the numbers across runs?

00:02:30 - Marcus Li: Good call. We show median and p95. For a given model and hardware combo, p95 can move a bit depending on batching and KV cache warmness. That's why the compatibility matrix is important: quantized model on T4 behaves differently than an A100 float16 run.

00:02:45 - 00:03:10 - Jonah Rivera: (screen) Here's the compatibility matrix. Columns are model families and quantization profiles: FP16, INT8, GPTQ-4bit, etc. Rows are hardware targets: A100, H100, T4, CPU. The cells show whether we have a validated execution path, approximate throughput (tokens/sec) and qualitative note like 'recommended', 'experimental', 'not supported'. For example, Llama-2-13B with GPTQ-4bit is validated on T4 and A100 but experimental on some older GPUs.
00:03:11 - Sara Kim: Do you handle automatic kernel selection or do we need to compile anything?

00:03:18 - Marcus Li: Runtime handles kernel selection and optimized execution path choices automatically. You can override for testing but production use we recommend the runtime's defaults. For private deployments we include the same runtime — so behavior is consistent.
00:03:30 - Priya Desai: Curious about accuracy regressions with quantization. Do you have guidance for evaluating quality loss?

00:03:36 - Marcus Li: Yes — our Optimize tooling runs delta-evals across your prompt set. It will compute per-prompt differences vs a float16 baseline and flag regressions above thresholds. We'll recommend quant profiles that hit your cost target while keeping quality drop within X% — you pick the threshold.
00:03:50 - Evan Ortiz: Are these deltas computed on your hosted infra or do we run them in our environment?

00:03:56 - Marcus Li: Both. For speed, we can run a hosted evaluation against your prompt set (no PHI ideally) or we can provide a self-hosted eval harness for Private deployments to run inside your VPC.
00:04:10 - Tom Reynolds: If we want to benchmark with real-ish data, we need the self-hosted path because of privacy. How heavyweight is that?

00:04:18 - Lena Park: For pilots we typically offer a lightweight containerized harness that runs inside your VPC with a small set of infra scripts. Marcus can follow up with the exact network requirements. That will also produce the same CSV style metrics we showed in the sheet.

00:04:30 - Marcus Li: Back to the Console — you can pin model variants per-route. For example, you can route triage (fast, cheaper) to a 7B quantized model and clinician-facing summarization to a 13B float16 model. We also support automatic fallback rules if capacity is constrained — route to a compatible variant with lower cost but acceptable quality.
00:04:50 - Priya Desai: Nice. What about latency SLOs when you enable batching to reduce cost?

00:04:56 - Jonah Rivera: You can set latency SLO targets and we tune batching policies. For sub-200ms SLOs we'd keep batch sizes small; for throughput-y jobs we allow larger batching. The Console shows token-level cost and expected latency impact per setting.
00:05:10 - Sara Kim: Let's talk integrations: SSO, audit logs, KMS. We need SAML + SCIM, plus audit logs to feed our SIEM. Does Private include KMS integration?

00:05:20 - Lena Park: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and we have SAML + SCIM for SSO provisioning. Audit logs are included and can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. We'll attach the SOC 2 docs and a security checklist after this call.
00:05:35 - Tom Reynolds: Great. Any constraints around data residency? Our infra sits in us-east-1 and we need keys and logs retained in region.

00:05:42 - Marcus Li: For Private it's under your management so residency is whatever your VPC/region dictates. For Hosted we offer region pinning for certain models — ask Marcus for the current model-region matrix.

00:05:55 - 00:06:40 - Jonah Rivera: (screen demo continued) API demo: Here's a simple text generation call using our SDK. You can pass a model id from the catalog, set a rollout policy, and enable streaming. Example shows model redwood/llama-med-13b-ptq with a pinned variant. The response shape supports tool-calling and structured output if you want JSON summarization templates.
00:06:41 - Priya Desai: Tool calling is interesting. Could we enforce structured output templates for clinician summaries?
00:06:48 - Marcus Li: Yes, we support schema validation hooks. The runtime can run a lightweight post-processor to enforce shape and reject outputs that don't conform.
00:06:55 - Evan Ortiz: Pricing question — how do you price quantized vs float runs?

00:07:00 - Lena Park: Hosted pricing is per-token with model-tier multipliers; quantized variants often fall into lower multiplier tiers. For Dedicated we do reserved capacity pricing with unit costs baked in. We'll include sample TCO in the spreadsheet for a typical 10M token/month workload.
00:07:15 - Tom Reynolds: For the pilot we want to run 2 weeks of benching with our prompts against 3 candidate models and 2 hardware profiles (A100 float16 and T4 quantized). Is that doable?

00:07:25 - Marcus Li: Yes that's standard. We'll provision a short Dedicated bench or run it in your Private env via the harness. We'll collect latency, p95, token cost, and quality deltas. Expect about 3-4 business days to get results once we have the prompts and access.
00:07:40 - Priya Desai: Ok timeline works. Security docs first though; legal needs SOC 2 and the encryption whitepaper.
00:07:47 - Lena Park: We'll send SOC 2 and the KMS/Network checklist today.
closing_notes: 00:07:50 - Lena Park: Recap: we'll share pricing + pilot SOP, Marcus will share the benchmark sheet and the compatibility matrix, Sara will coordinate VPC/network details and provide a prompt set. We'll target a pilot kickoff week of 2026-06-15 and delivery of initial bench results within a week of kickoff.
00:08:10 - Tom Reynolds: Sounds good. Thanks everyone. We'll watch for the spreadsheet and security docs.
00:08:20 - Lena Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
